gaps.location: pi_8a053dc873594d5de6593398, convexity lemma opening and theorem forward implication
gaps.issue: The context does not define polyhedral convex combinations, the admissible class for P_gamma, or the orthogonality property. The assertion that combinations centred inside a ray stay on that ray requires an incident-cell restriction; it is false for unrestricted barycentric combinations. Also, the proof establishes orthogonality only for bounded piecewise-affine obstacles, without establishing that these exhaust the required obstacle class or providing an approximation argument.

The lemma allows nonprimitive ray generators, but its proof uses slopes of t ↦ f(tu_i) in the intersection-theoretic mass formula without specifying a compensating weight normalization. Under the usual lattice normalization, take N=Z, u_1=2, u_2=-2, w_1=w_2=1, and f(x)=|x|. The displayed formula gives 4, whereas the Laplacian mass is 2. Primitive generators or an explicit alternative normalization are required.

No proof or supplied premise establishes that the envelope is itself an admissible continuous piecewise-affine function on a finite subdivision. This assertion is essential: the subsequent argument uses its outgoing slopes, atomic measure, and maximality against local perturbations. Compatibility of those perturbations with the source's piecewise-affine convention is also unspecified.

gaps.location: pi_8a053dc873594d5de6593398, corollary proof, eventual slopes and bounded difference
gaps.issue: The construction assumes that an arbitrary piecewise-affine reference has finitely many affine pieces and therefore eventual slopes. No supplied definition imposes global finiteness. A locally finite convex piecewise-affine function positive at infinity can have infinitely many increasing slopes, as with linear interpolation of t² at nonnegative integers. Thus the asserted eventual slopes and bounded difference require an explicit finiteness convention or additional hypotheses.

The bounded reference-shift proposition is neither stated nor proved in this item and is absent from the empty dependency context. Its identity, hypotheses, and preservation of the admissible obstacle class therefore cannot be checked. There is no eligible strict ancestor to request.
